intended: In cases one and three the height was recorded before the fertilizer was applied: 20 June precedes 3 August, and 19 April precedes 2 May. Half the evidence therefore describes growth that had already happened when the treatment was given, so it cannot be evidence for the treatment. The two remaining cases are not enough on their own.
reported: Two of the four cases have dates running backwards: the tomato was "fed 3 August" but measured "by 20 June", and the oak was "fed 2 May" but measured "by 19 April". The height gain is recorded before the fertilizer was applied.

reported: In two of the four cases the measurement date precedes the feeding date: the tomato was 'fed 3 August' but 'stood 11 cm taller by 20 June', and the oak was 'fed 2 May' but 'stood 13 cm taller by 19 April', while the other two (8 January to 26 February, 7 October to 24 November) run forward by about seven weeks. Half the reported gains are therefore recorded before the fertilizer was applied.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the particulate figures over the runs with the upgraded filter in service, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed. The claim is about the upgrade lowering particulate at the stack across its monitored period, so the population is every scheduled run at that stack and the figures describe three quarters of them. Bypass goes in under heavy load and upset conditions, which are the runs carrying the dirtiest gas, so a stack can post a lower figure over its in-service runs with its particulate across the period unchanged. The four stacks span four sites, four stack types, four quarters and four technicians, and the bypassed quarter is stated at each stack, so the same gap repeats in every case rather than being closed by any of them.
reported: The particulate numbers are a per-protocol slice: "The figures cover the runs with the upgraded filter in service, and a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed", so the worst quarter of runs is excluded from the post-upgrade figure while the "same unit a quarter earlier" baseline is not similarly filtered.

reported: The post-upgrade figures 'cover the runs with the upgraded filter in service' while 'a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed' and are therefore excluded, yet the comparison is to 'the same unit a quarter earlier', which includes all runs. Dropping the bypassed quarter of runs (the ones with no filtration at all) from the treated period alone could produce the 8-14 percent drop.

intended: The absence figures are tallied over "the pupils on the revised timetable throughout", while the same line records that "about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable". The claim is about absence in the cohorts that moved to the revised timetable, and that population includes the pupils who spent weeks back on the old schedule. Those pupils are the part of each cohort the change sat least firmly on, and their absence is precisely what the figures leave out, so the 4 to 7 percent falls are consistent with cohort absence not having moved at all. The four cases span four schools, four year groups, four terms and four registrars, and the same exclusion applies at each, so the spread of settings does nothing to repair the gap.
reported: Absence figures 'cover the pupils on the revised timetable throughout' while 'about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable', so roughly 20 percent of each cohort is excluded from the numbers. Pupils absent enough to miss the switch are precisely the high-absence group being filtered out, which alone could produce the 4-7 percent drop.

That fifth is excluded from the after-figure but included in the "term earlier" cohort baseline, so the 4-7 percent drop compares a filtered set of pupils against the full cohort.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the rates over the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and the clause beside it records that about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile. The claim is about board defects on the run, so the population is every board built on it and the defect figures describe nine tenths of that. Boards that take a pass on the old profile are the ones routed off the normal flow, and the extra handling and the extra heat cycle raise a board's defect risk on their own, so a rate built on the untouched boards alone sits below the run's own rate and the drops of 6, 4, 7 and 5 percent are consistent with defect production holding flat. All four runs are relay boards on the Aspen line inside March under operator Duarte, so one and the same exclusion sits under every case.
reported: 'Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile' - roughly 10 percent of each run's boards are dropped from the defect rate on a basis (mixed processing) that plausibly correlates with defects, so the 4-7 percent reduction covers a narrower board population than the run as a whole.

intended: The pass rates are tallied over "the students who attended every block", while the same line records that "about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block". The claim is about the cohorts given the tutoring blocks, so the population is every student in the cohort, not the full-attendance fraction alone. Students who attend every block are the steadiest students in a cohort and pass at higher rates whatever the tutoring did, so a 4 to 8 point rise can appear on that fraction with no change in what any student learned. The four cohorts span four colleges, four subjects, four terms and four tutors, and the same attendance restriction applies at each, so the spread of settings does not close the gap.
reported: The pass rates are per-protocol only: they "cover the students who attended every block" while "about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block" and are excluded. Full attenders are the more diligent quarter-to-three-quarters of the cohort and would out-perform the previous term's whole-cohort baseline regardless of the tutoring, so the 4-8 point gaps are not a like-for-like comparison.
